title: My Grandfather's Shop
topic: ประสบการณ์ส่วนตัว
lines: My grandfather has run a small hardware shop in our town for forty
years. When I was young, I thought **it** was the most boring place in the
world: dusty shelves, boxes of nails and old men talking about pipes.
Last summer, he hurt his back and asked me to help **him** for a month. I
agreed only because my parents insisted. On the first day, a woman came
in looking worried. Her kitchen tap was leaking, and she could not afford
a plumber. My grandfather spent twenty minutes drawing a picture to show
her how to fix **it** herself, and he sold her a part that cost 35 baht. A
week later, she came back with a bag of mangoes to thank him.
That kind of thing happened again and again. People did not just come to
buy things; they came for advice, and sometimes just to talk. I realized
that the shop was not really about selling. **It** was about helping people
solve problems. When the month ended, I asked if I could keep working on
Saturdays. My grandfather smiled. "I thought **you** might," he said.
